title: Smart routing: loop detection, variant tombstone health flags, and telemetry hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity-driven failover two weeks ago clients observed repeated cross-region reroutes and wrong-variant fallbacks that caused request amplification and increased tail latency. Root causes identified in the postmortem include (1) lack of per-request hop limits and telemetry to detect routing loops, (2) no TTL/tombstone on a model variant once flagged for fallback behavior, and (3) policy evaluation race conditions when multiple fallback rules apply simultaneously. This ticket implements three engineering controls: (A) request hop-count and loop-detection with an enforced max_hops header and an early-fail circuit breaker, (B) variant tombstone + health flags with automatic backoff and TTL to prevent rapid re-selection of recently-failed variants, and (C) richer routing telemetry & policy tracing (hop metrics, decision trace ids) to make future incidents observable and diagnosable. The work also includes integration tests and a staged rollout plan behind a feature flag. Goals/acceptance criteria: 1) Add hop_count header enforcement and metric sr.fallback.hop_count; when hop_count > 6 requests are rejected with 508 loop-detected, 2) Variant tombstones prevent re-selecting a variant for a configurable TTL (default 5m) after a circuit trip; metric sr.variant.tombstone.count emitted, 3) Policy evaluation emits sr.policy.trace_id and sr.policy.decision with sufficient context to reconstruct full routing tree in logs, 4) Integration tests (unit + e2e with local multi-region sim) validate loop and fallback behaviour, 5) Feature flag rollout (canary us-west-2 -> global) with rollback threshold: >3x baseline SR fallback rate or >1.5x baseline p99 latency, 6) Dashboards and alerts created on new metrics. Implementation notes: introduce hop_count on internal routing header X-RD-HOP-COUNT, increment on each router hop; add a small in-memory tombstone cache with cluster-wide invalidation via existing config topic; implement circuit-breaker heuristics: trip when N immediate fallbacks within window W (default N=5,W=60s). Backwards compatibility guarantee: if header absent, routers assume hop_count=0 and propagate header. Rollout: feature flag sr_loop_detection_v1 (default off) -> enable canary -> monitor 72h -> enable globally. See comments for timeline and follow-ups.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Incident summary posted to #incidents by Aisha Patel. Initial mitigation: temporarily disabled cross-region fallback policy for high-traffic routes to stop amplification.
2025-02-19 - Postmortem review with oncall, PM, and Design. Agreed to split work into telemetry + short-term mitigations and longer-term routing controls. Action owner: Liam Chen.

2025-02-21 - Short-term mitigation implemented: added server-side 'fallback cooldown' of 30s per-request for most-used variants. Reduced repeat fallbacks immediately but didn't eliminate loops when routers disagreed on policy evaluation ordering.
2025-02-24 - Design decision: use hop_count header + variant tombstone approach instead of global lockstep voting. Rationale: lower coordination overhead, faster to implement, measurable metrics.
2025-02-26 - Prototype submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721. Includes hop header and tombstone MVP + unit tests. Requesting review from Maya Singh and Javier Morales.

2025-02-28 - PR review notes: add deterministic trace ids for policy evaluation and ensure tombstone TTL is configurable via config service. Also add integration test simulating 3 router hops across regions.

2025-03-01 - PR updated with config knobs and added metric sr.fallback.hop_count. Load test (staging) shows no observable p99 increase with flag disabled; when enabled, loop-triggering scenario halts within 2 hops in staging sim.
2025-03-02 - QA schedule: integration test matrix created in TestRail (case SR-LOOP-001..SR-LOOP-006). Assign QA owner: Priya Nair.

2025-03-03 - Canary rollout started to us-west-2 behind sr_loop_detection_v1 flag. Monitoring dashboards created: /dashboards/sr-loop-detection and /alerts/sr-loop-detection-threshold. Initial 24h looked nominal.

2025-03-04 - Follow-up: observed a rare case where tombstone cache eviction raced with autoscaler rejoin; created ENG-13503 to add cluster-wide tombstone reconciliation and ENG-13504 to add chaos test for autoscaler churn. Liam assigned both.

Next steps: complete cluster-wide invalidation (ENG-13503), add chaos test and validate under instance churn (ENG-13504), finalize runbook and merge runtime PR. Owner: Liam Chen; PM review: Marco Alvarez.
notes: Key trade-offs: tombstone TTL prevents aggressive reuse but may slightly increase cold-start rate for variants; conservative default TTL=5m chosen. We prefer preventing amplification over perfect immediate capacity utilization. If this causes capacity pressure for small customers, we'll add per-customer TTL tuning in a follow-up.
